entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Abhishek Srivastava,Ajay Nand Pandey,Ashish Kaushik,Krishna Sha
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Mukesh Chandra Gupta,Shubham Prakash Gupta
Hon'ble Saurabh Srivastava,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. and perused the record.

2. It is submitted by learned counsel for applicant that the role of the applicant is only as worker who was instructed to collect the paper and deposit before the concerned company, whereas the siphoning of money in shape of withdrawal is permitted only to the merchant I.D which pertains to other co-accused who has already been granted bail vide order dated 29.1.2024 and as such the applicant is having no specific role with regard to allegation whatsoever has been put forward through the narration of the First Information Report, learned counsel for the applicant also submitted that the applicant is having no criminal history credited in his favour and he is languishing in jail since 21.2.2023 and in case he is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and will cooperate in the trial.

entities.text: Sagar Kumar vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, learned AGA although, vehemently opposed the prayer as made in the bail application but did not dispute the fact that the applicant is not having any criminal history credited in his favour.

It is also submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that criminal history of one case which was indicated by learned AGA and once the same has been inquired it revealed that in the first information report name of the father is different whereas name of the accused are same and only on this basis learned AGA submitted before the court that one case is pending as criminal history against the applicant.
4. Considering the fact that applicant has no criminal history to his credit, nature of offence,
evidence, complicity of the accused, submissions of learned A.G.A. and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, and the specific role with regard to receiving money was only possible with the merchant I.D and the same does not belong to the applicant.

5. The observation made above shall not be taken into consideration for any purpose at the time of trial by learned trial court, but at this juncture, learned counsel for the applicant made out a case for extention of bail in favour of the applicant and the same is allowed.
6. Let the applicant- Sagar Kumar involved in Case Crime No. 376 of 2022, under Sections 420, 409 IPC and Section 72 I.T. Act, Police Station Charthawal, District Muzaffar-Nagar be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to the following conditions:-
i.
The applicant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
ii. The applicant will not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witness.

iii. The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted and/ or the applicant shall make himself available for interrogation by a police officer as and when required.
iv.
The applicant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.

v. The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
vi. The applicant shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court.
vii. In the event, the applicant changes his residential address, the applicant shall inform the court concerned about new residential address in writing.
